# Buffered ambient-normal facet condition and exact interval removal

This note extends an ALREADY PROVED unbuffered theorem by retaining the
derivative of the invariant buffer norm. The unbuffered directional
formula, translated-zonoid inclusion, allocation quantifiers and
no-outside-facet consequence are in
`candidate 9c6d3cb586898f7e`,
independently audited in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
The new interval-removal argument below uses actual convexity and lattice
completeness. No higher-dimensional removal theorem or OC conclusion is
asserted.

## 1. Fixed mark and the displaced point in the normal derivative

Let C be a compact convex body with finitely many measured integer fibers
K_z of positive d-dimensional volume, d>=1. Mixed measure means the SUM
of their d-dimensional Lebesgue measures. Fix Y=(p,y), and let

    H(a,u)={a.(z-p)+u.(x-y)+delta G(u)>=0},
    G(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u), delta=epsilon f(Y)>0, u!=0,       (1)

where Sigma is positive definite. In this calculation the body, mark,
Sigma and scalar delta are FIXED. In particular this is cap-normal
variation, not body variation or mark variation. Assume (1) attains the
global buffered infimum at Y and its own fiber trace is proper. The same
necessary condition holds at an ambient-normal local minimum.

For D=(alpha,v), perturb (a,u) to (a+t alpha,u+t v). On the old cap plane
the margin derivative is

    ell_D(z,x)=alpha.(z-p)+v.(x-y)+delta DG(u)[v]
              =D.xi(z,x),
    xi(z,x)=(z-p,x-y+kappa),
    kappa=delta Sigma u/G(u).                              (2)

Equivalently the point used in the section moment is
Y'=(p,y-kappa), not Y. The Taylor remainder in the margin is O(t^2),
uniformly on the bounded measured set. Euler's identity gives

    (a,u).xi=0                                             (3)

on the old plane. Hence radial changes of the full normal are invisible,
as required by positive homogeneity. If normals are represented in the
chart G(u)=1, subtracting a multiple of (a,u) from a perturbation puts
it in that chart's tangent space without changing ell_D. Thus allowing
all D introduces no spurious direction.

## 2. All proper and supporting branches, including d=1

On every fiber classify the old plane as proper, inside supporting
(the entire fiber is captured), outside supporting (zero captured
d-volume), or strictly saturated. Let theta_P,theta_I,theta_O denote
the sums of H_(d-1) on the first three kinds of trace, divided by |u|.
A supporting trace of zero H_(d-1) measure contributes zero. For d=1
these are counting measures divided by |u|.

The EXACT right derivative of captured mass is

    D_H(D)=int ell_D dtheta_P
           -int (-ell_D)_+ dtheta_I
           +int (ell_D)_+ dtheta_O.                       (4)

For clarity, this formula does not put the closed-cap indicator on a
supporting face. Inside contact loses the negative-margin strip; outside
contact gains the positive-margin strip.

Here is an independent derivation. Rotate continuous coordinates so the
old normal is |u| times the last coordinate vector and integrate along
that coordinate. On each vertical line the convex fiber is an interval.
The moving cutting height has derivative -ell_D/|u| and a uniform O(t^2)
error. The derivative of the captured interval length is respectively
ell_D/|u|, min(ell_D,0)/|u|, max(ell_D,0)/|u|, or zero. Difference
quotients have one uniform bound on a bounded projection. Fubini and
dominated convergence give (4). For a proper cutting section, its
relative boundary has zero section measure and its relative interior
lies in the fiber interior. At a supporting section, its relative
interior admits an inward interval, by taking cones to an interior point.
Zero-area supporting sections vanish by the same argument. The uniform
O(t^2) margin error changes mass by O(t^2), using the uniform slab bound.
Closed nonvertical planes have zero d-volume, so no cap-plane volume
atom is omitted.

## 3. The exact buffered zonoid condition

Put m=int xi dtheta_P and, for theta=theta_I or theta_O, define

    Z(theta)={int q xi dtheta: q Borel, 0<=q<=1}.

These moment sets are compact and convex by weak-* compactness of the
bounded densities and finite-dimensional moment continuity. Their
support functions are int(D.xi)_+ dtheta. Therefore nonnegativity of
(4) for EVERY D is equivalent to

    -Z(theta_I) subset m+Z(theta_O).                        (5)

This is equivalence with absence of a strict FIRST-ORDER decreasing
normal; it is not a sufficient condition for an actual local minimum.
Its quantifiers are: for every prescribed inside density q_I there is
an outside density q_O with

    m+int q_I xi dtheta_I+int q_O xi dtheta_O=0.             (6)

Adding (4) at D and -D yields the necessary absolute-moment inequality

    int |D.xi| dtheta_O >= int |D.xi| dtheta_I.             (7)

More precisely, with the linear form

    B(D)=int D.xi dtheta_P
            +(1/2)int D.xi d(theta_I+theta_O),

the full first-order condition is

    |B(D)| <= (1/2)[int |D.xi| dtheta_O
                         -int |D.xi| dtheta_I]            (8)

for every D. Neither (7) nor (5) is arbitrary convex order.

If theta_O=0, (7) forces xi=0 theta_I-almost everywhere.
There is no own inside facet because the own trace is proper. Every
other measured fiber has z!=p, and its base component in xi is z-p!=0.
Thus theta_I=0. Equation (5) now gives m=0, so the summed proper-section
centroid is exactly Y'. In particular an actual positive-area INSIDE
supporting trace requires some actual positive-area OUTSIDE trace.

For a restricted space of normal motions the corresponding conclusion
is only that inside xi lies in the annihilator of that space. With ALL
ambient normals the preceding argument has no such exception. Base-only
perturbations already exclude the possible annihilator on a non-own
fiber. This does not assert pointwise matching or identify one outside
facet for each inside facet.

## 4. Inside contacts really can occur at a minimizing buffered cap

Take n=d=1, P={-1,0,1}, K_z=[-1,1], so C is the actual rectangle,
M=6, Sigma=1/3 and E_K(y)=2(1-y^2). Use L=1 and the usual invariant
factor f(y)=sqrt(E_K(y)/M). Fix 0<s<1/2 and set

    Y=(0,s), epsilon=3s/sqrt(1-s^2).

The physical threshold displacement epsilon f(s)G(1) is exactly s.
Every upward buffered cap is therefore

    x+a z>=0.                                             (9)

Its mass is exactly 3, for EVERY real a: central reflection of the
original mixed set exchanges its two open sides, and its boundary has
zero mixed one-dimensional measure. Every downward buffered cap is

    x<=a z+2s.

Its own interval contributes 1+2s. The two endpoint intervals contribute
at least 2: their thresholds are symmetric about 2s>=0, so reflection
at threshold zero and monotonicity suffice. Steep finite tilts attain
that lower bound. Pure-base caps at zero have closed mass4. Any further
containing threshold shift only increases the captured mass. Thus the
global buffered infimum at this fixed proper mark is exactly3.

The particular cap x+z>=0 has an INSIDE supporting endpoint at (1,-1),
an OUTSIDE supporting endpoint at (-1,1), and a proper own section at
(0,0). Here Y'=(0,0), m=0 and -Z(theta_I)=Z(theta_O), so the moment
inequality is attained exactly.

This disproves the assertion that inside supporting traces cannot
occur at a globally minimizing buffered cap. It does NOT disprove an
existential inside-free choice: other tilts in (9) are also minimizing.
Y is a fixed proper mark, not claimed to be globally deepest; indeed
the buffered depth at the middle centroid is strictly larger. The
example is strictly nonheavy (each fiber has mass2<M/2), but no joint
bad-minimum hypothesis is claimed.

## 5. Complete interval chains permit removal at no cost

There is an actual positive selection theorem when n=d=1. Let C be a
compact convex planar body whose positive integer fibers are intervals
at EVERY integer in a consecutive finite base P. Fix a proper mark and
an attained minimizing buffered cap with proper own trace. Then it
admits arbitrarily close equally minimizing caps having NO inside
supporting traces. More specifically, if the chosen cap has an inside
supporting trace, an arbitrarily small integer-tilt change makes ALL
its supporting traces strict, while preserving its mass exactly.

Reflect x if needed and scale the continuous normal to1. Hold that
normal fixed, so the buffer displacement does not change. Let the cap
line be x=q-a(z-p). Its intersection with C is a segment, because C
is convex. It is not a supporting line of C, since the own trace is
proper. Every fiber supporting contact is a boundary point of this
segment. By Section3 an inside contact forces an outside contact;
they occur at distinct bases because all fibers have positive length.
There are only two segment endpoints, so these are the ONLY supporting
contacts. Write their integer bases r<s. The proper own line point must
lie strictly between them: otherwise it would supply a third boundary
point or coincide with a nonproper fiber contact. Hence r<p<s.

Every integer fiber with r<z<s is cut properly, since the open segment
lies in int C. Every other measured fiber is strictly saturated. Put

    N=s-r-1>=1, c=(r+s)/2-p,
    P_1=sum_(r<z<s)(z-p)=N c.                             (10)

All proper-section densities are EXACTLY1. If r is the inside contact
and s the outside contact, the right derivatives in the +a and -a
directions are respectively

    (N+2)c,  -N c.                                       (11)

If their types are reversed, those derivatives are

    N c,  -(N+2)c.                                       (12)

Nonnegativity forces c=0 in either case. Thus the source base is exactly
the arithmetic midpoint (r+s)/2 and the proper base moment vanishes.

In (11) move a slightly DOWN: the inside trace becomes strict full and
the outside trace strict empty. In (12) move a slightly UP, with the
same effect. All old proper and strictly saturated statuses persist
for sufficiently small movement. On this one-sided cell each proper
interval cap length is affine in a, with total slope P_1=0; the other
lengths are constant. Hence the total captured mass remains EXACTLY
the old global minimum. The new cap has no supporting contacts.

This proof uses consecutive integer sampling, actual two-dimensional
convexity, and the common interval coarea1. Arbitrary fiber weights,
higher integer rank, or d>=2 do not retain this argument. In particular
it does not remove the inside-branch quantifier in the general mixed
body-response problem. The fixed-normal proper isolated minima in
`candidate 714bee9248df3ce6`
concern a different selection issue and remain valid.

## 6. Scope

The general buffered necessary condition is the norm-corrected form of
an archived theorem. The interval selection theorem is a bounded
additional geometric consequence. The companion
`candidate 777caee80bc87e0e`
now gives an actual d=2 obstruction to inside-free selection at a fixed
proper mark and a definite positive buffer: its minimizing halfspace
is unique and retains an inside facet. Global deepestness and the
small-epsilon regime are explicitly outside that example. No averaged zonoid inequality is promoted
to convex order, no body-motion separator is inferred from cap-normal
stationarity alone, and no Gamma payment follows from these statements.

Supplementary checker:
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_buffered_normal_facet_and_interval_removal_two_sided.py`,
**14,950 exact checks PASS**. It checks the norm-dependent one-fiber
derivative branches, the actual rectangle's two orientations, exact
supporting statuses, the full consecutive-integer derivative identities,
and compatible sheared-interval calibrations. The all-normal statements
and interval removal follow from the proofs above, not the sampled
parameter checks.
